reuse.why: The change reuses recurrence conversion and weekend adjustment helpers, but each consumer separately assembles the skip-versus-move policy.

duplication.why: Occurrence resolution is repeated across four consumers, and the forward and reverse working-day searches duplicate their filtering and limit logic.

placement.why: Holiday classification belongs in shared schedules and handler registration belongs in the server app, but scheduling policy remains scattered into consumers.

scope.why: The edits stay focused on the requested scheduling changes, their consumers, tests, types, and release notes.

maintainability.why: Shared holiday matching is straightforward, but repeated policy orchestration, separate search limits, and untyped new configuration parameters increase maintenance costs.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange, and schedule-template.ts independently implement occurrence resolution outside getNextDate, despite its role as the shared next-date abstraction.

disguised_duplication.where: The skip-versus-move decision appears as search selection in getNextDate, nested branches in getUpcomingDates, continue-based filtering in getDatesInRange, and paired local closures in schedule-template.ts.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter; getNextDate adds daily-specific forward search, reverse search, and adjustment exclusion branches; upcoming dates, range dates, and budget enumeration independently orchestrate the same policy.
